correctness.rationale: Geometrically the divisor comprises 3n distinct lines, three ordinary n-fold family concurrency points and n² ordinary triple points. A normalization has 3n disjoint P1 components. Ordinary r-fold local gluing contributes torus rank r-1 and unipotent dimension (r-1)(r-2)/2, giving u=n²+3(n-1)(n-2)/2. The branch-incidence bipartite graph has V=3n+n²+3, E=3n(n+1), so H1 graph rank 2n²-2. In nonsplit q≡-1 mod n with odd n, Frobenius inversion fixes exactly 7 vertices/6 edges comprising a tree, and a paired-edge invariant spanning tree makes the integral cycle lattice a direct sum of n²-1 regular two-dimensional permutation modules. This establishes isomorphism (not just isogeny) to Weil restriction tori. Descent of truncated principal-unit groups uses p>n. Normalization branch-orbit counts produce stated zeta factors and q^m-point counts. Independent projective-point enumeration verified (n,q)=(5,11),(5,19),(7,13),(7,29); sampled checks are not the all-n proof. The source verifier additionally checks finite invariant graph trees and orbit incidence.

value.rationale: The exact integral arithmetic torus of a singular line arrangement is a useful structural invariant; distinguishing a Weil restriction isomorphism from an isogeny gives finite rational Picard groups. The nonsplit n-independent 3q+1 count and all-extension zeta are natural global consequences, not arbitrary enumerated slices.

final_claim: For odd Ceva divisor degree 3n (n≥5 odd, char p>n) in the q≡±1 mod n regimes, Pic^0 is split unipotent Ga^{n²+3(n-1)(n-2)/2} times a split torus Gm^{2n²-2} or a nonsplit induced torus (Res_{Fq²/Fq}Gm)^{n²-1}; corresponding rational point groups and full zeta functions are explicit, with nonsplit #D_n(Fq)=3q+1.
limitations: Odd n≥5, char>n, q≡±1 mod n; neither arbitrary Frobenius action nor even n proved.
